title: The girl who fell three kilometres and walked out of the jungle
hook: A plane broke apart over the Peruvian jungle in 1971, and a girl fell three kilometres and lived.
summary: In 1971 seventeen-year-old Juliane Koepcke fell about three kilometres from a broken airliner, then followed a stream for ten days to reach loggers, the only survivor of 92.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica / Wikipedia: LANSA Flight 508, 24 Dec 1971, struck by lightning over Peru, 91 of 92 aboard died; Juliane Koepcke, 17, fell about 3,000 m strapped in her seat row.
Juliane Koepcke's own account and interviews (BBC, Guardian): parents were zoologists, she followed a stream downstream for about ten days and found a loggers' hut.

lines.text: In nineteen seventy-one, a plane broke apart over the Peruvian jungle.
lines.caps: In *1971, | a plane *broke apart | over the *jungle

lines.text: Seventeen-year-old Juliane Koepcke fell three kilometres, strapped to her seat.
She woke alone in the forest. Everyone else was gone.
Her parents were scientists, and had taught her one rule.
Follow the water, because streams lead to rivers, and rivers lead to people.
lines.caps: Follow the *water, | streams lead to *rivers, | rivers lead to *people

lines.text: So she waded downstream, barefoot and half blind, for ten days.
lines.caps: She waded *downstream, | barefoot, *half blind, | for *ten days

lines.text: Then she found a hut, where loggers helped her.
lines.caps: Then she found a *hut, | where *loggers helped

lines.text: She was the only survivor of ninety-two people aboard.

post.caption:
She fell from the sky, then walked out alone, using one rule her parents taught her.
Would you have known to follow the water?
